headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Users
short_summary: This bill reallocates certain grid infrastructure costs to large energy users like data centers, aiming to reduce residential electricity bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, Senator Louise Lucas, Delegate Destiny LeVere Bolling, Dominion Energy (initially).
opponents: Data center industry, large manufacturers, business advocacy groups.
news_headline: Governor Amends Bills Shifting Data Center Costs
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393 and SB 253, which aim to shift more energy costs onto data centers and large manufacturers to save residential customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics, including Dominion Energy, expressed concerns that the Governor's amendments might weaken the original goals of the legislation.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities to publicly report data centers' monthly water consumption, increasing transparency for resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local governments.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality, making the information publicly available. This aims to provide transparency regarding the industry's water consumption, a growing concern for communities and environmental groups.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill mandates site assessments for new data centers to evaluate noise impact on nearby residences and schools, and allows localities to consider other environmental effects.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, Delegate Joshua Thomas, environmental groups, local governments.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry, business advocacy groups.
news_headline: New Siting Requirements for Virginia Data Centers
news_summary: HB 153 introduces new siting requirements for large data centers, mandating impact assessments on agriculture, parks, and historical sites before rezoning approval. Lawmakers view this as a step towards stronger regulations on where data centers can be built and their effects on surrounding communities.
